summary: safeGit now returns a GitResult object with code, stdout and stderr instead of a stdout string, and no longer throws on failure. The GitResult type is also exported from the core package.

findings.title: Callers still treat the safeGit result as a string
findings.problem: safeGit now returns a GitResult object, but currentBranch in packages/cli/src/branch.ts:7 still calls name.trim() on it. changedFiles in packages/cli/src/status.ts:7 still calls out.split() on it.
findings.consequence: currentBranch catches the TypeError and always returns null, so the CLI always exits with 'not a git repository'. In changedFiles, the TypeError is not caught, so it rejects.
findings.fix: Update currentBranch and changedFiles to read result.stdout. Have them check result.code, since safeGit no longer throws.

findings.title: Failure signal moved from a thrown error to a return code
findings.problem: currentBranch relies on safeGit throwing to detect a missing repository. safeGit now catches every failure and returns a nonzero code instead.
findings.consequence: Outside a repository, currentBranch's catch never runs, so currentBranch cannot return null for that case. The CLI then reports failed git output as a branch name instead of exiting.
findings.fix: Make currentBranch return null when result.code is nonzero. Make changedFiles handle a nonzero result.code too.

findings.title: Changed safeGit behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: safeGit changed its return shape and its error handling. No test file in the repository exercises safeGit.
findings.consequence: Nothing caught the broken callers, and future regressions in safeGit will also go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests that check safeGit's success and failure results. Add tests that check how currentBranch and changedFiles handle those results.
